after.AM: The tricolour belonged to the short-lived First Republic of 1918–1920. Soviet annexation suppressed it; the Armenian SSR restored it in 1990, before independence the following year.
after.AO: The half cogwheel represents industrial workers; the machete stands for farming and the independence struggle. Their arrangement echoes a Soviet-era emblem.
after.AR: The Sun of May has 32 rays, alternating straight and wavy. It recalls both the Inca sun god Inti and a sunlit moment during the independence movement.
after.AU: The five stars form the Southern Cross. A larger seven-pointed star nearby represents the federation's original states and its territories.
after.AZ: The crescent evokes Islamic and Turkic heritage. The star's eight points are variously linked to branches of the Turkic peoples or letters in an older script.
after.BA: Parliament could not agree on a replacement after the war, so international High Representative Carlos Westendorp selected the 1998 design. European blue and gold were meant to be acceptable to all three constituent peoples.
after.BB: The emblem comes from Neptune's trident on a colonial badge, but its shaft is missing. That break is understood as a symbol of independence.
after.BD: The disc is moved toward the hoist so it looks centred when the flag flies. It evokes a rising sun and those who died in the liberation war.
after.BH: The five points refer to the Five Pillars of Islam. The white area also recalls a nineteenth-century peace treaty that changed the earlier red banner.
after.BI: The stars are often linked to the national motto: Unity, Work, Progress. The white cross stands for peace between the red and green sections.
after.BN: The white and black bands represent two traditional chief ministers. Yellow is the sultan's colour, while the red emblem includes a parasol, crescent and hands.
after.BW: The band evokes a zebra and is widely read as racial harmony. The blue field represents rain, precious enough to appear in the national motto: 'Let there be rain.'
after.CF: Republic founder Barthélemy Boganda designed the flag as a link between France and Africa. It combines French and Pan-African colours and survived the change from autonomy to independence.
after.CI: Its orange-white-green order is the reverse of Ireland's green-white-orange flag. The resemblance has occasionally confused observers, although the two designs arose from different histories.
after.CM: The green-red-yellow tricolour predates the central star. The star was added as a symbol of unity between regions once administered by France and Britain.
after.CY: The map is coloured like copper, a metal associated with the island since antiquity. The two olive branches below it call for peace between its communities.
after.CD: The 2006 constitution brought back a design close to one used in the 1960s, but with a lighter sky-blue field. In between, the country had flown the very different flag of Zaire.
after.DJ: The independence movement's banner became the national flag in 1977. Its blue and green bands were chosen to acknowledge two major communities, the Issa Somalis and the Afars, while the white triangle calls for peace.
after.DM: Designed by Alwin Bully for independence, the flag was revised in 1981, 1988 and 1990. The changes refined the parrot's orientation and surrounding details; the sisserou remains one of the rare named bird species on a national flag.
after.ER: The red triangle remembers lives lost in the independence struggle. The gold olive wreath was adapted from an earlier autonomous-region flag and stands for peace.
after.ES: Charles III chose red and yellow for ships because they were easier to distinguish at sea than other monarchies' mostly white flags. The design later spread to land use.
after.FI: The precise blue shade and proportions were fixed by a flag law in 1978. The older Nordic cross links the flag to its neighbours, while blue and white evoke lakes and snow.
after.GB: The upright red cross is St George's for England; the white diagonal cross is St Andrew's for Scotland; the red diagonal cross is St Patrick's for Ireland.
after.GD: The small nutmeg fruit nods to a major spice crop. Six stars around the red border represent the original parishes, and the central star stands for the capital.
after.GT: The bird on the central emblem is a quetzal, a symbol of liberty. It sits above a scroll bearing the independence date, with crossed rifles and swords behind it.
after.IQ: The green inscription reads 'God is the Greatest'. It first appeared in a leader's handwriting in 1991; the angular Kufic-style lettering replaced that version in 2008.
after.IR: The border inscription repeats 'God is the Greatest' 22 times, marking a date of the 1979 revolution. The central emblem can be read as the word Allah and as a tulip.
after.JM: The gold diagonal cross divides the field into four triangles. Green recalls lush vegetation and hope; black now stands for strength and creativity, though it once referred to hardships.
after.KE: A traditional shield and crossed spears express defence of the people, land and freedom. The narrow white stripes among the main colours represent peace.
after.KI: Instead of keeping a colonial badge in a small corner, the new nation enlarged its old coat of arms to fill the flag. The frigatebird, waves and sun came from that earlier Gilbert and Ellice Islands emblem.
after.KP: Its formal name means 'Blue and Red-coloured Flag of the Republic'. The large red band refers to revolutionary tradition, while the blue bands are associated with sovereignty and peace.
after.KM: This is the seventh national design since independence. Four stars and stripes refer to the archipelago's islands, including Mayotte, which remains administered by France but is still claimed by the Comorian state.
after.KZ: Artist Shaken Niyazbekov's entry won a competition with more than a thousand proposals after independence. The design also draws on older steppe traditions, including an eagle and a 'ram's horns' ornament.
after.LA: The white disc can be read as a full moon over the Mekong River and a sign of unity. The red bands remember lives lost in the struggle for independence.
after.LS: The black mokorotlo is a traditional Basotho straw hat. Blue, white and green together express the national motto: 'Peace, Rain, Prosperity.'
after.LU: The colours come from medieval Luxembourg arms showing a red lion against white and pale-blue stripes. The lion is absent from the everyday national flag.
after.MA: The plain red field has been linked to the Alaouite dynasty since at least the seventeenth century. The later green interlaced star is known as the Seal of Solomon.
after.MH: Emlain Kabua, then the first lady, designed the flag. Its two diagonal bands stand for the Ratak ('sunrise') and Ralik ('sunset') island chains.
after.MN: The Soyombo emblem contains a flame for prosperity, a sun and moon for endurance, and shapes representing honesty and friendship. It was created in the seventeenth century.
after.MR: The green field with crescent and star was the original design. Two red bands were added in 2017 to honour those who resisted colonial rule.
after.MV: The crescent represents Islam, the green panel peace and the islands' palms, and the red border those who died defending the country.
after.MZ: The book stands for education, the hoe for agriculture and the rifle for defence and the liberation struggle. It is the only national flag depicting a modern firearm.
after.FM: The earlier Pacific trust-territory flag had six stars for six districts. The four stars here represent the federation's four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae.
after.NA: A constituent-assembly committee considered more than 870 public entries before independence. It combined liberation-movement colours with new white borders and a sun to give the flag a broader national identity.
after.NL: The earlier Prince's Flag was orange, white and blue. Red gradually displaced orange during the seventeenth century, possibly because its dye lasted better at sea.
after.NP: Its stacked pennants recall two former ruling houses and the Himalayan peaks. The moon and sun express the hope that the country will last as long as they do.
after.PW: The disc is a full moon, traditionally a good time for fishing, planting and celebrations. The blue field symbolises self-government rather than the ocean.
after.PY: The front carries the national arms with a star and wreath; the reverse carries the Treasury seal. Very few national flags have different emblems on their two faces.
after.PK: The earlier Muslim League banner supplied the green field and crescent. At independence a white band was added for religious minorities, expressing the aim of a state for citizens of different faiths.
after.PS: The black, white and green bands recall three historical caliphates. The red triangle traces to the Hashemite-led Arab Revolt and is also associated with the struggle for self-determination.
after.PT: After the monarchy fell in 1910, a commission replaced its long-used blue and white with the republicans' green and red. The central armillary sphere still ties the new flag to the country's maritime past.
after.SA: Because the inscription is the shahada, the Islamic declaration of faith, this flag is never lowered to half-mast. It is made so the sacred words read correctly on both sides; the sword recalls the modern state's founder.
after.SB: A New Zealand artist's sketch was adapted after a public contest. Its five stars first meant the main island groups; the country now has nine provinces, but the original count remains.
after.SD: Artist Abdel Rahman Ahmed Al-Jali won a public competition after the 1969 revolution. The new flag replaced a blue-yellow-green one and used colours associated with Arab liberation movements.
after.SO: The blue field first honoured the United Nations, which administered a trust territory before independence. The five star points refer to five regions inhabited by ethnic Somalis.
after.SS: The design came from the Sudan People's Liberation Movement, which fought a long civil war. It already flew over the autonomous south before becoming the flag of the independent state in 2011.
after.SY: The three red stars have been linked to Aleppo, Damascus and Deir ez-Zor. This former independence flag returned after decades under other designs.
after.TN: Created for the Beylik of Tunis after a naval defeat, the design remained through the French protectorate and independence. Its proportions were later standardised without replacing the familiar emblem.
after.VN: Originally made for an uprising in 1940, this design later flew for North Vietnam. It became the flag of the reunited country in 1976; its star is often read as a union of different social groups.
after.SG: A committee led by Toh Chin Chye had just two months to finish the design. An early three-star proposal became five stars, now linked to democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality.
after.SL: Adopted at independence in 1961, this design has remained unchanged. Its blue band can recall the natural harbour of the capital, while green and white refer to land, unity and justice.
after.SR: Jacques Herman Pinas won a design competition as independence approached. Green and red drew on leading political parties; white came to stand for justice and rights, yellow for the future.
after.ST: The stars refer to the two main islands, while the green and yellow stripes evoke their vegetation and tropical sun. The design grew from an independence movement's banner.
after.TM: The five woven motifs represent traditional tribal designs. Olive branches below them were added to mark the country's declared permanent neutrality.
after.TJ: When former Soviet republics adopted new flags, this one alone in Central Asia kept red from its Soviet predecessor. The crown and seven stars instead point toward older Persian and Tajik traditions.
after.TT: Artist Carlisle Chang created the diagonal-band design for an independence committee. Its red, white and black have been interpreted as fire, water and earth.
after.UG: The grey crowned crane is the national bird. Its raised leg suggests progress; the bird had earlier been a badge of local soldiers under British rule.
after.US: Fifty stars represent the current states, while thirteen stripes remember the original colonies. Since 1818 the law has provided for a new star when a state joins.
after.UZ: Adopted just months after independence, it was the first new flag among the post-Soviet Central Asian republics. Its blue also recalls the banner associated with the medieval ruler Amir Timur.
after.VC: Swiss graphic artist Julien van der Wal designed the replacement for a flag carrying a breadfruit leaf. His three diamonds suggest a V and recall the islands' nickname, the 'Gems of the Antilles'.
after.VU: The independence party Vanua'aku Pati supplied the basic colours and layout. Designer Kalontas Mahlon added a form that follows the island chain and symbols of prosperity and peace.
after.WS: The design began under New Zealand administration with four stars. A smaller fifth star was added in 1949, thirteen years before independence, and the flag stayed when the country's name changed in 1997.
after.ZA: Chosen for the first non-racial democratic election, this design was supposed to last only five years. The 1996 constitution kept it permanently; its converging lines are often read as a shared path.
after.ZM: At independence the flag reused an eagle from the colonial-era coat of arms but gave it a new meaning: rising above difficulties. Even its orange shade, associated with copper, was adjusted in 1996.
after.ZW: The bird is adapted from stone sculptures found at Great Zimbabwe, linking the modern flag to older heritage. The white triangle around it represents peace.
